newsitem.title: UK: Abbey says working on final ScotAm offer.
newsitem.headline: Abbey says working on final ScotAm offer.

text.p: Britain's Abbey National said on Friday that it was working with Scottish Amicable towards making a final offer for the mutually-owned life assurance group.

Abbey National triggered a takeover race for Scot Amicable after its more than 1.4 billion pound ($2.30 billion) approach for the group was outbid by a 1.9 billion pound offer from Prudential Corp Plc earlier this week.
"Abbey National has started to work with Scottish Amicable in order to ensure that its final offer fully values policyholders' interests as well as the interests of the staff," the British bank said.
It said it would take account of the most recent financial information which Scottish Amicable intends to provide to all bidders.

Abbey added: "We expect the decision-making process from here on to be confidential and we are certain that our final offer will represent the best long term value to Scottish Amicable and its policyholders". Its offer includes an immediate minimum payout of 400 million pounds to policyholders in cash or Abbey shares.

ScotAm's immediate response was to denounce it as both "vague" and "inadequate" and said it intended to press ahead with its two-stage plans to drop its mutual status and float the group over the next three to five years. ($1=.6097 Pound)
